stem:
Consider the following dynasties of Ancient India:
1. Shunga 2. Maurya
3. Kushana 4. Kanva
Which of the following is the correct chronological order of their rule?
expl: Scholars consider the Mauryan Empire to have lasted from approximately 321 BCE to 184 BCE. The Shunga Dynasty is believed to have lasted from approximately 184 BCE to 73 BCE. The Kanva Dynasty spanned approximately 73 BCE to 28 BCE. The Kushan Empire is believed to have existed between the first and third centuries CE. Therefore, the correct chronological order of the dynasties of ancient India is as follows: Maurya → Shunga → Kanva → Kushan

Match List I with List II
List-I List-II Places in Ancient Presently in which India State a. Karmasuvarna 1. Maharashtra b. Pragjyotish 2. Gujarat c. Girnar 3. West Bengal d. Pratishthan 4. Assam
Select the correct answer using the codes given below: A B C D
expl: Archaeological and historical accounts describe Karnasuvarna as an ancient city, believed to be located in present-day Murshidabad district, West Bengal. Ancient Sanskrit literature uses the names Pragjyotisha and Kamarupa to refer to ancient Assam and its surrounding region. Mount Girnar and its associated ancient religious and historical sites lie in the modern-day state of Gujarat. Pratishthan (Paithan) is a town in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (formerly Aurangabad) district of Maharashtra state, located on the banks of the Godavari River.

stem: Which inscription tells about the various achievements of Rudradaman-I?
expl: An inscription of Rudradaman I has been found at Junagadh (Gujarat). The same rock on which it is engraved also contains a copy of Ashoka’s fourteen major rock edicts and an inscription of Skandagupta. It is written in pure Sanskrit and in the Brahmi script. It throws light on Rudradaman’s various achievements

stem: According to the rock inscription in Sanskrit, composed around the second century CE, Sudarshan Lake, an artificial reservoir, was repaired by

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The Junagadh inscription of Rudradaman I (130–150 CE) has been found from Girnar Hill in Gujarat. This Sanskrit inscription is among the early Sanskrit inscriptions. From it, we get information about the construction and reconstruction of the dam of Sudarshana Lake.

stem: Who among the following first issued gold coins on a large scale?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The introduction of gold coinage on a large scale by the Kushana rulers was their most important contribution to the Indian subcontinent. Vima Kadphises is credited with starting the circulation of gold coins.

stem: In pre-Gupta times, a large number of lead coins were issued by the

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: In the pre-Gupta period, a large number of lead coins were issued by the Satavahana rulers. It may be noted that the Satavahana dynasty was founded by Simuka. Their actual capital was Pratishthana (Paithan). In the Puranas, this dynasty is called Andhrabhritya or of Andhra origin.

stem: Which dynasty ruled over India after the Shunga dynasty?
expl: The last Shunga king, Devabhuti, was killed through the conspiracies of his minister Vasudeva. The new dynasty founded by Vasudeva came to be known as the Kanva or Kanvayana dynasty. Like the Shungas, it was also a Brahmin dynasty.
